relations.subject: vector-index:composite-vector-index
relations.evidence: A key difference between Hyperscale and Composite Vector indexes is how they handle scalar values in queries. Hyperscale Vector indexes compare vectors and scalar values at the same time. Composite Vector indexes always apply scalar filters first, and only perform vector searches on the results.

relations.subject: vector-index:composite-vector-index
relations.evidence: Use Composite Vector indexes when you want to perform searches of documents using both scalars and a vector where the scalar values filter out large portions of the dataset.

relations.subject: vector-index:search-vector-index
relations.evidence: If your dataset will not grow beyond 100 million documents and you need to perform hybrid searches that combine vector searches with other Search Service features, such as text or geospatial search, use a Search Vector Index.

cross_product_finding: This page's comparison table cites explicit Couchbase Server engine version numbers (8.0, 8.0, 7.6) for the three vector index types' availability, on a Capella (cloud/) page - the same anomaly already flagged in cloud/search/search-index-params.json and cloud/n1ql/n1ql-language-reference/createindex.json/createvectorindex.json elsewhere in this repo. This is now confirmed as a recurring, not isolated, pattern specifically within the vector-index/ and search/ content families: unlike most other Capella surfaces (roles, credential types), vector/search feature-gating content appears to be authored against/copied from the underlying Couchbase Server version rather than translated into a Capella-native availability concept. Reusing version:server-8.0 (already minted) and adding version:server-7.6 to keep this consistent for the coordinator to reconcile in one place.
